title: Utilizing calcite‐bound phosphate to reconstruct historical phosphorus loading to marl lake ecosystems
content:
Abstract

Reconstructing historical phosphorus (P) concentrations in lakes has been a long-standing problem for paleolimnology. The most commonly applied method is the use of diatom-inferred total P models, but there are well-documented limitations to these approaches. Authigenic calcite co-precipitated with P is a promising geochemical indicator of ambient P conditions in the water column through time. We tested two approaches for isolating the P content associated with authigenic calcite. The first capitalizes on a well-known sequential extraction method but incorporates a physical separation to increase the specificity of the extraction. The second uses scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) to target P concentrations of authigenic calcite. These methods were evaluated using calcite-rich sediments from Utah Lake in north-central Utah, USA. Utah Lake is a eutrophic lake with a well-documented increase in P pollution due to rapid population growth and wastewater inputs. Both methods showed increased up-core concentrations of calcite-P that match historical P loading records; however, a relatively high P detection limit reduced the effectiveness of the semi-quantitative SEM-EDS method. Overall, we demonstrate that the methods outlined here are feasible for reconstructing historical P concentrations in lakes with sufficient sedimentary authigenic calcite and appropriate sedimentary environments.
